statement: The function returns a result r and r is the minimum possible bitwise OR of the remaining array after at most k operations. Explicitly, for a partition P given by 0 = p0 < p1 < ... < pm = n with m >= 1, define V(P) = (nums[p0] & ... & nums[p1-1]) | ... | (nums[p_{m-1}] & ... & nums[p_m-1]). Then r = min { V(P) : P is such a partition and n - m <= k }. Here & and | are 64-bit bitwise AND and OR on nonnegative values.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 10^5, 0 <= nums[i] < 2^30 for every i with 0 <= i < n, and 0 <= k < n.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not panic, overflow, or otherwise fail.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 10^5, 0 <= nums[i] < 2^30 for every i with 0 <= i < n, and 0 <= k < n.

statement: The returned result r satisfies r >= 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 10^5, 0 <= nums[i] < 2^30 for every i with 0 <= i < n, and 0 <= k < n.

statement: The returned result r satisfies r < 2^30.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 10^5, 0 <= nums[i] < 2^30 for every i with 0 <= i < n, and 0 <= k < n.

statement: Let O = nums[0] | nums[1] | ... | nums[n-1]. The returned result r satisfies r | O = O; equivalently, every bit position that is 1 in r is also 1 in at least one nums[i].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 10^5, 0 <= nums[i] < 2^30 for every i with 0 <= i < n, and 0 <= k < n.

statement: Let A = nums[0] & nums[1] & ... & nums[n-1]. The returned result r satisfies r & A = A; equivalently, every bit position that is 1 in A is also 1 in r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 10^5, 0 <= nums[i] < 2^30 for every i with 0 <= i < n, and 0 <= k < n.

statement: There exists a partition of nums into m nonempty contiguous blocks, with n - m <= k, such that the bitwise OR of the bitwise ANDs of those blocks equals r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 10^5, 0 <= nums[i] < 2^30 for every i with 0 <= i < n, and 0 <= k < n.

statement: For every partition of nums into m nonempty contiguous blocks with n - m <= k, if W is the bitwise OR of the bitwise ANDs of those blocks, then r <= W.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 10^5, 0 <= nums[i] < 2^30 for every i with 0 <= i < n, and 0 <= k < n.

statement: There exists a partition of nums into exactly n - k nonempty contiguous blocks such that the bitwise OR of the bitwise ANDs of those blocks equals r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 10^5, 0 <= nums[i] < 2^30 for every i with 0 <= i < n, and 0 <= k < n.

statement: If k = 0, then r = nums[0] | nums[1] | ... | nums[n-1].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 10^5, 0 <= nums[i] < 2^30 for every i with 0 <= i < n, and 0 <= k < n.

statement: If k = n - 1, then r = nums[0] & nums[1] & ... & nums[n-1].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 10^5, 0 <= nums[i] < 2^30 for every i with 0 <= i < n, and 0 <= k < n.

statement: The returned result r satisfies r = min over 1 <= s < n of ((nums[0] & ... & nums[s-1]) | (nums[s] & ... & nums[n-1])).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 10^5, 0 <= nums[i] < 2^30 for every i with 0 <= i < n, and k = n - 2.

statement: If there exists a value c such that nums[i] = c for every i with 0 <= i < n, then r = c.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 10^5, 0 <= nums[i] < 2^30 for every i with 0 <= i < n, and 0 <= k < n.

statement: Let r1 = min_or_after_operations(nums, k1) and r2 = min_or_after_operations(nums, k2). Then r1 >= r2; allowing more operations cannot increase the minimum achievable OR.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 10^5, 0 <= nums[i] < 2^30 for every i with 0 <= i < n, and 0 <= k1 <= k2 < n.
